instruction: Design a college student dashboard with attendance tracking functionality.
input: The dashboard should include a student profile, attendance records, notifications, and a settings section. The dashboard should be accessible and responsive on both desktop and mobile.
output: The dashboard should consist of the following pages: Home, Profile, Attendance, Notifications, and Settings. Each page will have specific UI components and information displayed. instruction: Design a student profile page with academic performance for a college management system.
input: The page should include a student's academic performance details such as GPA, courses taken, and grades. It should also allow the student to view their academic history and edit personal information.
output: The student profile page will be divided into two main sections: 'Profile Information' and 'Academic Performance'. The layout will be as follows: The top section will display the student's profile information including their name, photo, and current academic year. Below this, the 'Academic Performance' section will have a grid of cards, each representing a semester. Each card will display the semester name, GPA, and a list of courses with grades. The page will also include a 'History' button to view the student's academic history and a 'Settings' button to edit personal information. The color palette will be a light blue (#ADD8E6) with darker shades (#87CEFA) for emphasis. The typography will be 'Roboto' with a font size of 16px for the main content and 14px for labels. Users will be able to edit their personal information and grades. Validation will ensure that grades are numeric and GPA is between 0 and 4. The page will be responsive, with the card grid collapsing into a list on mobile. Error messages will appear for invalid inputs. The page will be accessible, with sufficient color contrast and alt text for images.

instruction: Design an admin dashboard for a college management system focusing on student statistics and charts.

instruction: Design a student fee payment and fee history page for a college management system.
input: The page should include a fee payment form, a history section displaying payment details and status, and a summary of fees.
output: The student fee payment and fee history page will be designed with a clear and intuitive layout. The color palette will be a combination of blue and green, with blue for the main content and green for the payment buttons. instruction: Design a college examination timetable interface for students and faculty.
input: The interface should display upcoming exams, their dates, times, and rooms. It should allow users to filter by day, week, or month, and to view detailed schedules for specific days. Users should be able to register for exams and view their own schedules.
output: The interface will be organized into a header, content area, and footer. The header will include navigation links to the main pages, such as Home, My Schedules, and Filter. The content area will display the examination timetable. The footer will include links to important college resources and a feedback form for users to report issues or suggestions. The design will use a color palette of light blue (#ADD8E6) and dark blue (#00008B). The typography will be a sans-serif font for the header and footer, and a serif font for the content area. Users can interact with the content area by filtering by day, week, or month, and by selecting specific days to view detailed schedules. They can also register for exams and view their own schedules. Error handling will be implemented for invalid input, and the interface will be responsive for both mobile and desktop devices. The interface will be accessible, with proper color contrast, keyboard navigation, and screen reader support. Users will be notified of errors and will be able to retry the operation if necessary.

instruction: Design a student assignment submission dashboard for a college management system.
input: The dashboard should allow students to view their assignments, submit their work, and track the submission status. It should also provide feedback on submitted assignments and allow for communication with instructors.
output: The student assignment submission dashboard will be a single-page application with a responsive layout. The layout will consist of a header, navigation menu, main content area, and a footer. The header will include the college logo, navigation links, and a search bar for quick access to specific assignment details. The navigation menu will provide access to different sections of the dashboard, such as 'My Assignments,' 'Submit Assignment,' and 'My Feedback.' The main content area will display the relevant information and functionality for each section. The footer will include links to important college resources and a contact form for students to communicate with instructors. The navigation menu and footer will be fixed in position on all pages, while the header and main content area will adjust based on the screen size. The color palette will consist of a primary color (a shade of blue) and a secondary color (a shade of gray). The typography will use a sans-serif font for body text and a serif font for headings. The user interactions will include submitting assignments, viewing submission status, and receiving feedback. The validation will ensure that required fields are filled out and that file uploads are of the correct type and size. The interface will be designed to be accessible, with appropriate ARIA labels and keyboard navigability. Error handling will provide clear error messages and suggest solutions, such as providing a list of valid file types or file size limits. The dashboard will be fully responsive, ensuring a seamless experience for students on both desktop and mobile devices. On mobile devices, the navigation menu will be displayed as a hamburger menu, and the main content area will stack vertically. The header and footer will remain fixed, and the main content area will adjust to fit the screen width. The interface will be designed to be user-friendly, with clear and concise labels for all buttons and fields, and the feedback system will be designed to provide students with detailed information on their submissions and any necessary revisions.

instruction: Design a faculty course and class management interface for a college management system.
input: The interface should allow faculty to manage courses and classes, including creating, editing, and deleting courses, as well as adding and removing students from classes. It should also display course schedules, student information, and class attendance records.
output: The interface will have a navigation bar at the top with links to different sections such as Home, Courses, Classes, and Settings. The main content area will have a header displaying the current page title and a footer with links to important pages. Below the header, there will be two main sections: the left side will display a list of courses and classes, and the right side will display detailed information for the selected course or class. The header will also have a search bar to filter the list of courses and classes. The footer will include links to settings and a logout button. The color palette will be a light blue with dark blue accents. The typography will be a sans-serif font. Users can create, edit, and delete courses and classes by clicking on the corresponding buttons in the left side. Adding and removing students from classes will involve clicking on the student's name in the list and selecting the appropriate action. Users can view course schedules, student information, and class attendance records by clicking on the corresponding buttons in the right side. The interface will be responsive and will adjust to fit mobile and desktop screens. On mobile devices, the navigation bar will be fixed at the top, and the list of courses and classes will be displayed in a scrollable list. Error handling will be implemented for invalid inputs and missing information, and accessibility features will be included for users with disabilities such as screen readers and keyboard navigation.

instruction: Design a college library book search and issue tracking page
input: Create a detailed, practical design specification for a college library book search and issue tracking page.
output:
The design specification for the college library book search and issue tracking page includes the following details:

1. Page Layout and Component Placement:
- The page layout consists of a header, search bar, list of books, issue details section, and footer.
- The header includes the college library logo and navigation links.
- The search bar is placed at the top of the page for easy access.
- The list of books is displayed in a scrollable table format.
- The issue details section includes a form for issuing books and a history section for tracking issues.
- The footer contains links to important pages and contact information.

2. Important UI Components and Displayed Information:
- The search bar allows users to input keywords for book search.
- The list of books displays book title, author, and availability status.
- The issue details section includes fields for user name, book title, issue date, return date, and issue status.
- The history section shows previous issue and return records.

3. Color Palette and Typography:
- The color palette includes a primary color (a shade of blue) for headings and buttons, and a secondary color (a shade of gray) for background and borders.
- The typography uses a sans-serif font (Roboto) for body text and a bold sans-serif font (Roboto Bold) for headings and buttons.

4. User Interactions and Validation:
- Users can search for books by entering keywords in the search bar.
- The search results are dynamically updated based on the input.
- Users can issue books by filling out the form and clicking the 'Issue' button.
- The form includes validation for required fields (user name, book title, issue date, return date).
- The form also includes validation for the issue date being before the return date.
- The issue history is updated in real-time as issues are added or removed.

5. Responsive Behavior on Mobile and Desktop:
- On mobile, the page layout adjusts to a single-column layout with the header, search bar, and footer fixed at the top and bottom.
- On desktop, the page layout is a two-column layout with the header, search bar, and footer fixed at the top and bottom.
- The list of books and issue details section are scrollable on mobile.
- On desktop, the list of books is displayed in a scrollable table format.
- The issue form is displayed in a modal on mobile.

6. Accessibility and Error Handling:
- The page is designed with accessibility in mind, including ARIA labels for elements and sufficient color contrast.
- Error messages are displayed for invalid inputs, such as empty fields or invalid date formats.
- Keyboard navigation is supported for users who cannot use a mouse.
- Screen readers are supported to provide a text alternative for images and interactive elements.

instruction: Design a student result and grade report dashboard for a college management system.
input: The dashboard should display results and grades for students, including subject names, grades, and scores. It should also show a summary of the semester's performance.
output: The dashboard will be divided into three main sections: a header, a central content area, and a footer. The header will contain the logo and navigation links, while the footer will have links to other important sections of the system. The central content area will feature a table displaying the student's results and grades. Each row of the table will show the student's name, subject name, grade, and score. The table will be sorted by subject name and grade. The summary of the semester's performance will be displayed below the table. This section will show the overall average score, highest and lowest grade, and the number of subjects passed. The color palette will be a combination of light blue and dark blue. The typography will be a sans-serif font. Users can sort the table by subject name, grade, and score. The interface will be responsive, ensuring a good user experience on both desktop and mobile devices. On mobile devices, the table will be displayed in a single column, and the summary section will be displayed below the table. The interface will be accessible, with clear labels for buttons and forms. Error handling will be implemented for form submissions, displaying appropriate error messages if the user inputs are invalid. For example, if a user tries to submit a form without entering any data, an error message will be displayed, indicating that all fields are required.

instruction: Design a college admission application tracking interface for a college management system.
input: The interface should allow students to track their applications, view application status, and communicate with admissions offices. It should also provide parents the ability to monitor their children's application progress.
output: A detailed design specification for the college admission application tracking interface is as follows. The interface is designed to be user-friendly, responsive, and accessible. It is divided into several key components, including a navigation bar, application progress page, application details page, and an application history page. The navigation bar is located at the top of the interface and includes links to different sections such as 'My Applications', 'Parent Monitoring', 'Application Status', and 'Communications'. The application progress page displays a list of all applications with their current status, such as 'Submitted', 'Under Review', 'Approved', and 'Declined'. Each application has a detailed view button that leads to the application details page. The application details page shows the application form, submission date, status, and any comments or messages. The application history page displays the entire history of each application, including all communication and status changes. The color palette used in the interface is a combination of blue and white, with a shade of light blue for buttons and links. The typography used is a clean, readable font. Users can interact with the interface by clicking on buttons, selecting options, and typing in text boxes. The interface validates user inputs to ensure data integrity. For example, the application form validates that all required fields are filled out before submitting. The interface is designed to be responsive, with a fluid layout that adjusts to different screen sizes. The interface is also designed to be accessible, with features such as keyboard navigation, screen reader support, and sufficient color contrast. Error messages are displayed in a clear, user-friendly manner to help users understand what went wrong and how to correct it. The interface is designed to support both desktop and mobile devices, with a responsive design that ensures a smooth user experience on all devices.

The page layout will be designed for both desktop and mobile devices, ensuring a seamless user experience across all platforms.
